checklist_item.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is the gas cap value 16777216 identical at both enforcement points?

code_scope.resolution_error: Prysm is a consensus layer client and does not implement an execution-layer txpool. The value 16777216 in Prysm is HISTORICAL_ROOTS_LIMIT (SSZ beacon state constant at config/fieldparams/mainnet.go:10), semantically unrelated to gas caps. No txpool gas cap enforcement code exists in this codebase.

audit_items.state_context: Prysm is a consensus layer (CL) client implementing the Ethereum beacon chain. Transaction validation and txpool gas cap enforcement are handled entirely by execution layer (EL) clients (go-ethereum, Nethermind, Besu, Reth, Erigon). Prysm treats execution payloads as opaque data from the EL via Engine API.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: Prysm contains no txpool implementation and no gas cap constant at 16777216 used for transaction validation. The value 16777216 appears only as HISTORICAL_ROOTS_LIMIT in SSZ beacon state config (config/fieldparams/mainnet.go:10, config/params/mainnet_config.go:139). There are no two enforcement points to compare for consistency.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.cache_analysis: No txpool cache exists in Prysm. N/A.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.concurrency_analysis: No concurrent transaction validation exists in Prysm. N/A.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: No code path exists in Prysm that performs gas cap enforcement at 16777216. No symbolic variables, no comparison operators, no counterexample construction is possible.
phase2_symbolic_execution.timing_dependencies: None. No code to race against.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: The code under test does not exist in Prysm. No entry point leads to txpool gas cap enforcement.
phase2_5_reachability_analysis.attack_surface: None. Prysm is a consensus client. Gas cap enforcement is an EL client responsibility.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: The invariant (gas cap value consistency across enforcement points) cannot be evaluated because neither enforcement point exists in Prysm.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: N/A — no guard exists because the subsystem does not exist in this codebase.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: Prysm is a consensus layer client and does not implement an execution-layer txpool. The gas cap constant 16777216 does not exist as a transaction validation parameter in Prysm. This item is categorically out-of-scope for this target.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: Re-target this check to an EL client (e.g., go-ethereum, Nethermind, Besu, Reth) where txpool gas cap enforcement is actually implemented.

checklist_item.title: Is a rejected transaction dropped and never forwarded to block building?

code_scope.resolution_error: Prysm is a consensus layer client and does not implement an execution-layer txpool. There is no transaction submission, rejection, or forwarding logic in Prysm.

audit_items.state_context: Prysm does not maintain a transaction pool. Block building is triggered via the Engine API to an EL client (e.g., engine_getPayloadV4). Prysm never makes accept/reject decisions about individual EL transactions.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: Prysm has no txpool. No transaction submission, rejection, or forwarding logic exists. State leakage from a rejected transaction is impossible in a system that never accepts transactions.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.cache_analysis: No transaction state cache exists in Prysm.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.concurrency_analysis: No concurrent transaction handling exists in Prysm.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: No symbolic path exists for transaction submission to Prysm. There is no function accepting user transactions, no rejection logic, and no forwarding path to block building within Prysm.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Prysm does not expose a txpool API. External actors cannot submit transactions to Prysm directly.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: The invariant (rejected transactions are never forwarded) cannot be evaluated because Prysm does not implement transaction ingestion or forwarding.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: Out-of-scope. Prysm does not implement a txpool. Transaction acceptance and forwarding is an EL client concern.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: Re-target to an EL client (go-ethereum, Reth, Nethermind) where transaction lifecycle management is implemented.

checklist_item.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is the comparison operator <= (not <) used for gas cap check?

code_scope.resolution_error: Prysm does not implement txpool gas cap comparison. The only gas-related comparison in Prysm is in config/proposer/loader/loader.go for block gas limit target validation (not transaction gas cap enforcement).

audit_items.state_context: Gas limit in Prysm context refers to the block gas limit target a validator proposes for its beacon blocks' execution payloads. This is entirely different from the EL txpool per-transaction gas cap (16777216) which limits individual transaction gas limits in the mempool.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: No gas cap comparison operator (<=, <, >, >=) exists in Prysm for transaction gasLimit validation at 16777216. The proposer loader comparison (config/proposer/loader/loader.go:336-342) validates block gas limit target configuration, not transaction-level gas caps.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: No symbolic path through a gasLimit <= 16777216 comparison exists in Prysm. The off-by-one property (whether <= or < is used) cannot be evaluated against absent code.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: No gas cap comparison code exists in Prysm for transaction validation at 16777216.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Invariant (comparison operator is <=) cannot be evaluated; the comparison does not exist in Prysm.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: Out-of-scope. Prysm does not implement txpool transaction gas cap comparison. This is an EL client concern.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: Re-target to an EL client where the comparison operator can be inspected. Focus on the boundary case gasLimit = 16777216 to check for off-by-one errors in the EL client's txpool acceptance logic.

checklist_item.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Do all clients use identical comparison semantics (> not >=)?

code_scope.resolution_error: Prysm is a consensus layer client and does not participate in EL txpool transaction validation. Cross-client txpool comparison semantics are an EL concern only.

audit_items.state_context: Cross-client txpool inconsistency could theoretically cause different EL clients to accept/reject the same transaction, but this is an EL protocol concern. Prysm's role is consensus layer only — it depends on the connected EL client to perform all transaction validation. Prysm does not compare notes with other CL implementations on txpool policies.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: Cross-client txpool comparison semantics are an EL-layer concern. Prysm does not validate transactions and therefore has no comparison semantics to evaluate. Prysm does not participate in txpool transaction acceptance/rejection consensus.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: No transaction submission path exists to Prysm. Cross-client consistency of Prysm's non-existent txpool cannot be measured.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Prysm does not participate in EL txpool transaction validation. Cross-client inconsistency at the consensus layer is a separate domain (fork choice, attestation processing, block validation).

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Cross-client txpool invariant cannot be evaluated against Prysm because Prysm has no txpool.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: Out-of-scope. Prysm is a CL client. Cross-client txpool comparison semantics (> vs >=) at the 16777216 boundary are an EL concern involving go-ethereum, Nethermind, Besu, Erigon, and Reth.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: Re-target to EL clients. Cross-client fuzz testing of txpool acceptance boundaries (gasLimit = 16777216 boundary) should be run against EL clients directly. A single-transaction test with gasLimit = 16777216 submitted to all EL clients simultaneously would reveal comparison semantic differences.

checklist_item.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is RLP encoding of gasLimit strictly validated across all clients?

code_scope.resolution_error: Prysm does not perform RLP decoding of EL transactions. The only RLP usage in Prysm is ENR record encoding for P2P peer discovery (beacon-chain/p2p/utils.go:45), which is unrelated to transaction encoding or gasLimit validation.

audit_items.state_context: Prysm receives execution payloads from the EL client via engine_getPayloadV* calls. These payloads contain already-validated transactions as raw byte arrays. Prysm never decodes individual transactions from their RLP encoding. Non-canonical RLP attacks target EL clients directly, not Prysm.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: Prysm does not perform RLP decoding of execution layer transactions. The only RLP usage in Prysm is ENR record encoding for peer discovery (beacon-chain/p2p/utils.go:45), which is unrelated to transaction encoding. EL transactions arrive at Prysm as opaque byte arrays from the connected EL client via the Engine API.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: No RLP transaction decoding path exists in Prysm. Crafted non-canonical RLP transactions cannot be submitted to Prysm and would never reach Prysm's transaction handling layer because no such layer exists.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: RLP transaction decoding is performed by the EL client, not Prysm. Prysm treats execution payloads as opaque data structures received from the EL via Engine API.
phase2_5_reachability_analysis.attack_surface: None. Non-canonical RLP transaction crafting is an attack against EL clients, not Prysm.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: RLP encoding uniformity invariant cannot be evaluated in Prysm because Prysm does not decode EL transaction RLP.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: Out-of-scope. RLP transaction encoding and validation is performed entirely by EL clients. Prysm's only RLP usage is ENR peer record encoding (beacon-chain/p2p/utils.go:45), which is unrelated to transaction validation.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: Re-target to EL clients (go-ethereum, Reth, Nethermind, Besu, Erigon). Non-canonical RLP transaction fuzzing should be run against those clients' txpool and block import paths, particularly crafting transactions with leading zeros or oversized integer encodings for gasLimit near the 16777216 boundary.
